video_metadata.working_title: IOWA 1979 Cold Case Solved After 39 Years — Justice for Michelle Martinko
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: An 18-year-old Cedar Rapids senior was stabbed to death in her family's car at a brand-new mall on 19 December 1979; the killer's own blood, saved for 39 years, was traced through a stranger's genealogy upload to a man nobody had ever suspected, Jerry Lynn Burns, arrested on the 39th anniversary and convicted in 2020.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: Grief turning into awe: the victim fought so hard that she left the clue that solved her own murder.

protagonist._instructions: The main character of your story - can be hero, villain, or antihero. Fill with verified facts only.
protagonist.full_name: Michelle Marie Martinko (victim and narrative heart); antagonist: Jerry Lynn Burns (convicted)
protagonist.age_at_time_of_events: Michelle: 18 (born 1961). Burns: 64 at arrest in December 2018 (some reports say 65 later), which makes him about 25 in December 1979 (derived arithmetically).
protagonist.occupation_or_status: Michelle: senior at Kennedy High School, Cedar Rapids. Burns (in 2018): owner of Advanced Coating Concepts, a powder coating shop on the south side of Manchester, Iowa.
protagonist.location: Cedar Rapids, Linn County, Iowa; Burns lived and worked in Manchester, about 45 miles north.
protagonist.physical_description: Michelle: blonde hair worn in the Farrah Fawcett style of the era, described by friends as stylish (Find a Grave, single source).
protagonist.background_brief: Younger of two daughters of Albert F. Martinko and Janet Martinko (née Zillig); older sister Janelle. Above-average student well regarded by school officials; made the twirling squad as a sophomore, which was nearly unheard of; twirled baton at football halftime shows; sang in the Kennedy women's choir and the Concert Choir; performed in theater productions; planned to study interior design at Iowa State University.
protagonist.psychological_profile: Described as polite and reserved as a child, responsible and diligent at school; friends called her stylish and kind. No speculation beyond this.
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: On her last evening she went to pick up a winter coat that had been put on layaway (one source says her mother had placed it there), carrying $180, after her choir's banquet.

victims_or_targets._instructions: People affected by the protagonist's actions. Include 3-5 key figures minimum.

individuals.name: Michelle Martinko
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: No documented connection to Burns; investigators described the killing in 1979 as 'personal in nature'; family says the why is unknown.
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Stabbed to death in her family's Buick on 19 December 1979.
individuals.humanizing_detail: Baton twirler, choir singer, theater performer, future interior design student.

individuals.name: Albert F. Martinko
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Died without knowing who killed his daughter (John Stonebraker's statement).
individuals.humanizing_detail: Reported his daughter missing with his wife around 2 a.m.

individuals.name: Janet Martinko (née Zillig)
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Died without knowing who killed her daughter (Stonebraker statement).
individuals.humanizing_detail: One source says she had placed the winter coat on layaway.

individuals.name: Janelle Stonebraker (née Martinko)
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Waited about 40 years for an answer; became the family's public voice.
individuals.humanizing_detail: Wished her parents could have seen the verdict.
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: "We don't know exactly the why's and some of the details, but we definitely know who did it" (24 Feb 2020).

individuals.name: John Stonebraker
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Read the family's victim impact statement by video on 7 Aug 2020.
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: Burns would "forfeit his freedom forever and die alone."

collective_victims_if_applicable.group_description: The Cedar Rapids community, and in particular dozens of people who lived under suspicion or rumor for decades; DNA cleared numerous potential suspects and even people who confessed.
collective_victims_if_applicable.total_number_affected: More than 125 DNA samples were collected over the life of the case (single source [44]).
collective_victims_if_applicable.range_of_impacts: Fear, rumor, suspicion of innocent people, a case the local paper and TV called one that 'haunted' the city.

chronological_timeline._instructions: List every significant event with exact dates when possible. This is the backbone of your script.

events.what_happened: Michelle Marie Martinko is born (exact date not verified).

events.date: early December 1979 (less than two weeks before 19 Dec)
events.what_happened: Westdale Mall opens.
events.significance: Brand-new mall becomes the crime scene.

events.what_happened: Michelle attends the Kennedy Concert Choir banquet.
She drives the family's tan 1972 Buick Electra alone to the mall to finalize the purchase of a winter coat on layaway, carrying $180; the car is parked near JCPenney.
Last time anyone remembers seeing her, reportedly outside a jewelry store.
Her parents report her missing.

Police find Michelle dead inside the family Buick. She had been stabbed many times (CBS: 29 stab and cut wounds) and had defensive wounds on her hands. She was fully clothed, not sexually assaulted and not robbed. No weapon or fingerprints were found. Investigators call the killing 'personal in nature'.
events.significance: Discovery; blood evidence on the gearshift and her dress is preserved.

events.what_happened: Numerous potential suspects, and even people who confessed, are investigated; DNA later clears them. More than 125 DNA samples are collected over the years.
A male DNA profile is developed from the killer's blood on evidence from the car/dress and uploaded to CODIS. No match.
events.significance: The killer's genetic fingerprint exists but has no name.

events.what_happened: DNA fingerprinting is discovered (background); five years after the murder.
events.significance: In 1979 the bloodstains could not identify anyone.

events.date: Trial testimony, 2020 (status as of the search)
events.what_happened: None of about 14 million profiles in CODIS matched the crime-scene blood.
Cedar Rapids police hire Parabon NanoLabs to predict ancestry, eye, hair and skin color, freckling and face shape from the DNA.
events.significance: First use of the new science.

events.what_happened: Police release Parabon Snapshot composite images to the public.
Golden State Killer suspect arrested through GEDmatch genealogy (background).
Investigators learn they can use genetic genealogy; Parabon tells them about GEDmatch.

A GEDmatch match leads to Brandy Jennings' family line; two branches of the tree are excluded with covert samples; the third branch yields a cousin sharing DNA; Parabon concludes the source is likely one of three brothers: Ken, Don and Jerry Burns. A brother's straw from a golf course clubhouse and another's toothbrush from curbside trash are excluded.
Denlinger watches Jerry Burns drink several sodas through a clear plastic straw; Burns leaves the straw; police collect it without a warrant.
Lab reports the straw's 'DNA donor could NOT be eliminated as the major contributor' to the crime-scene profile.

On the 39th anniversary, Denlinger and Detective J.D. Smith, in plain clothes, interview Burns at his business for over an hour with a camera hidden in a coffee mug. Burns denies involvement, keeps taking work calls, and without being asked mentions missing anchor Jodi Huisentruit. A warrant swab of his mouth is taken.
On a recorded ride, Burns says it is possible to block things out of your memories.
Burns, 64, is arrested and charged with first-degree murder; held in the Linn County Jail on a $5 million cash-only bond; Chief Wayne Jerman announces the arrest.
events.significance: Arrest exactly 39 years after the night of the killing.

events.what_happened: Lab confirms Burns' swab matches the dress DNA; probability of a random unrelated match 'less than 1 out of 100 billion'. Burns pleads not guilty.
Suppression hearing; the court refuses to throw out the straw DNA.
Jury selection and trial begin.
Denlinger testifies; former 1979 investigators describe the scene; DNA expert ties the blood to Burns.
State rests after playing Burns' interview video.
After closing arguments and about three hours of deliberation, the jury finds Burns guilty of first-degree murder.
Sentencing reset (to June); ultimately held in August.

Judge Fae Hoover-Grinde denies a new-trial motion and sentences Burns to the mandatory life in prison without parole; $150,000 to Michelle's estate; Burns says somebody else did it; John Stonebraker's video statement.
Burns hires appellate attorney Kathleen Zellner.
EFF files an amicus brief challenging the surreptitious DNA collection.
5-2 decision (Justice David May) affirms: the straw left on the Pizza Ranch table was abandoned; analyzing DNA from it was not an unconstitutional search. Justices McDermott and Oxley dissent.
Petition for certiorari (No. 23-206) denied.

Burns files a petition for postconviction relief alleging ineffective counsel, that a cellmate testified falsely to get a lighter sentence, that counsel opened the door to improper expert testimony on male DNA, and that counsel failed to present evidence pointing to Michelle's former boyfriend.
The State asks the court to dismiss, saying the claims were not raised on direct appeal.

events.date: 20 Apr 2027 (scheduled; exact date reported by two secondary sources)
events.what_happened: Postconviction relief trial scheduled.
events.significance: Status as of Oct 2026: pending, no ruling found.

cold_open_material._instructions: The most dramatic moment of your story - this will be your hook.

the_moment.exact_date: Wednesday 19 December 1979, evening; discovery about 4 a.m. Thursday 20 December
the_moment.exact_location: Westdale Mall parking lot, southwest Cedar Rapids, Iowa
the_moment.what_is_happening: An 18-year-old leaves her choir banquet to pick up a winter coat at a mall that opened less than two weeks earlier.
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: She is found stabbed to death in her family's Buick; no weapon, no fingerprints, no witness.
the_moment.ironic_twist: She fought so hard that the killer cut himself; his blood stayed on her dress and the gearshift for 39 years, and he was arrested 39 years to the day after the night she died.

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: Who killed Michelle Martinko in a crowded Christmas-season mall lot, and how could his own blood stay nameless for 39 years?

the_method._instructions: How did the protagonist do what they did? Technical details that can be explained to a general audience.
the_method.technique_name: Investigative genetic genealogy (forensic genetic genealogy) with covert reference sampling
step_by_step_explanation: 1979: blood from the attacker is preserved on Michelle's dress and the car's gearshift.
2006: a male DNA profile (STR profile) is developed and searched in CODIS: no match.
2017: Parabon NanoLabs predicts physical traits (Snapshot) and police release composites.
May 2018: police learn genealogy can be used; the DNA is converted into a SNP file and uploaded to GEDmatch, a public genealogy database.
The match list includes a distant cousin, Brandy Jennings, who uploaded to learn about her father's side.
Genealogists build family trees back to shared great-grandparents and forward to living men of the right age and place.
Covert samples exclude two branches; a third branch points to three brothers.
Discarded items exclude two brothers (golf clubhouse straw; toothbrush).
29 Oct 2018: Jerry Burns' Pizza Ranch straw is collected; the DCI lab cannot exclude him as the major contributor.
19 Dec 2018: a warrant swab confirms; random-match probability less than 1 in 100 billion.
the_method.why_it_worked: The killer's blood had been preserved, and by 2018 enough ordinary people had placed their DNA in a public database for a distant cousin to appear.

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: The FBI-run national database of DNA profiles from convicted offenders, arrestees and crime scenes; it only helps if the killer is already in it.
A public genealogy website where people upload their own DNA results to find relatives.
Relatives who share great-grandparents (or are a generation apart from that level); they share only a small slice of DNA.
Prediction of appearance traits from DNA; produces a likeness, not an identity.
The legal idea that once you voluntarily throw something away in public, you lose your privacy claim to it.

the_method.scale_of_operation: More than 125 DNA samples over the case; 14 million CODIS profiles searched without a hit; three family branches; three brothers.

systemic_failure._instructions: What institution, system, or authority failed to prevent this?
systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: Not a single negligent agency; the limits of 1979 forensic science and of databases that only contain known offenders.
systemic_failure.how_they_were_supposed_to_protect: Identify the killer from evidence at the scene.
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: No DNA technology in 1979; no weapon, no fingerprints, no witness; the killer had no profile in CODIS; years of focus on suspects who DNA later cleared.
specific_incompetence_examples: DNA cleared numerous potential suspects and even confessions [22] (no claim of misconduct verified)
2006 profile sat in CODIS with no hit for 12 years [11][12]
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The man convicted lived about 45 miles away and ran his own business for decades; he was never a suspect until a stranger in Washington State uploaded her DNA.

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Cedar Rapids Police Department with the Iowa Division of Criminal Investigation (DCI) lab and Parabon NanoLabs
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: Investigators believed the attack was 'personal in nature'; community rumor focused on people who knew her, including a former boyfriend who was never charged.
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: GEDmatch match to Brandy Jennings in 2018.
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: Leaving a straw on a Pizza Ranch table on 29 Oct 2018 (and, in 1979, bleeding at the scene).

the_confrontation._instructions: The arrest, raid, or climactic moment when everything collapses.
the_confrontation.location: Advanced Coating Concepts, Manchester, Iowa; then a police car to Cedar Rapids
the_confrontation.scene_description: Two plain-clothes officers; a camera hidden in a coffee mug; an interview of more than an hour; a cheek swab.
the_confrontation.protagonist_reaction: Denied involvement; showed little emotion; took work calls; mentioned Jodi Huisentruit unprompted; on the ride said it was possible to block things out of your memories.
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: The arrest fell on the 39th anniversary, a date Denlinger chose.

legal_resolution.trial_date_if_applicable: February 2020 (began week of 10 Feb; verdict 24 Feb 2020)
legal_resolution.notable_court_testimony: Investigator Denlinger on the genealogy and straw; former 1979 investigators on the scene; DNA expert on the strength of the match; the hidden-camera and car-ride videos; a jailhouse witness (cellmate) whose testimony Burns now says was false (allegation, unproven).

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: Burns would "forfeit his freedom forever and die alone." His mark on the world would be a short notice: "Convicted Martinko murderer dies in prison."
victim_impact_statements.emotional_impact: Michelle's parents died without knowing; she was 'her own best witness'. He noted Burns cannot be put to death because Iowa has no death penalty, and said the family was at peace with that (paraphrase) [28].

legal_resolution.sentence_received: Life in prison without the possibility of parole (mandatory in Iowa for first-degree murder); $150,000 to Michelle's estate.
legal_resolution.protagonist_statement_in_court: "First of all, I'd like to say that somebody else stabbed Michelle to death in that car that night. I don't know who. I don't know why." ... "And I would like to thank my family and friends for their support."
legal_resolution.current_status: As of October 2026: conviction affirmed by the Iowa Supreme Court (31 Mar 2023, 5-2); U.S. Supreme Court denied review (10 Oct 2023). Burns, who maintains his innocence, filed a postconviction relief petition in late April 2026; the State moved to dismiss (May 2026); a PCR trial is reported scheduled for 20 April 2027 in Linn County. No ruling found. Reported to be held at Anamosa State Penitentiary (single weak source; not used in script).

universal_stakes.why_this_matters_to_viewer: A teenager on an ordinary errand; a killer who was never on any list; a family who waited 40 years.
universal_stakes.how_this_could_happen_to_them: Every viewer has made a solo trip to a parking lot at night; every viewer has relatives whose DNA may be in a public database.
universal_stakes.lesson_or_warning: Preserve evidence: a stain kept in a lab in 1979 became the answer in 2018. And the privacy debate: what we leave behind in public can be tested.
universal_stakes.current_relevance: The 2023 Iowa Supreme Court ruling on abandoned DNA is cited in the national debate on covert DNA collection; postconviction litigation is pending in 2026-2027.
